chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, said,
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not from us, the one who does not revere our elderly and show mercy to our young ones.'
ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about respecting the elderly and young in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise yet profound definition from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), linking social etiquette (adab) directly to theological identity (shi'iyya). This hadith is frequently cited in Shia jurisprudence and ethics to establish that reverence for the elderly and compassion for the youth are not merely cultural norms but essential markers of belonging to the Ahl al-Bayt's community. It underscores the integration of vertical spiritual authority with horizontal social cohesion within the Shia tradition.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, raising it, said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is not from us, the one who does not revere (respect) our elderly and being merciful to our young ones’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad in a marfu’ manner from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever does not consider our elders as dignified and does not show kindness to our people who are yet to grow up, is not from our people.”
